title: Little's law
text: The average number of requests in progress equals the arrival rate times the average time each request spends in the system: L = lambda x W.

title: Occupancy rate
text: The occupancy rate is the share of capacity that is busy on average. Close to 100 percent, the queue and the wait grow very fast.

title: Docker layer cache
text: Each instruction in a Dockerfile makes a layer. When nothing changed above a layer, Docker reuses it from the cache instead of running the instruction again.

title: Named volumes
text: A named volume keeps the database files outside the container, so the data survives when the container is stopped, removed or rebuilt.

title: pgvector
text: pgvector is a Postgres extension that stores embeddings and finds the nearest vectors, which is how a search service finds similar documents.

title: Health checks
text: A health endpoint tells the platform whether the service is ready. A good one checks the dependencies the service cannot work without, like its database.

title: Secrets
text: Passwords and API keys never go into Git or into an image. Pass them at run time through environment variables or a secret store.

title: Rate limits
text: A model provider caps how many requests you may send per minute and how many may run at once. Above that cap, more copies of your service only wait longer.
